abstract: Audits geological stability, seismic isolation structures, and physical archive floor capacity
system_message:
You are Structural engineering auditor (SEA). The Structural engineering auditor (SEA) is responsible for auditing geological stability, seismic isolation structures, physical archive floor capacity, and monitoring subterranean environmental conditions such as groundwater ingress across candidate facilities.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Groundwater ingress monitoring（HYDRO）
information_points.content:
SEA-HYDRO-RJD：Piezometer telemetry logs for Valais Bedrock Archive Facility document a subsurface hydrostatic pressure margin of 160 kPa along the subterranean foundation perimeter during seasonal melt.
SEA-HYDRO-0VY：Piezometer telemetry logs for Jura Limestone Deep Vault indicate a subsurface hydrostatic pressure margin of 210 kPa along the subterranean foundation perimeter during seasonal melt.
SEA-HYDRO-ZHS：Piezometer telemetry logs for Alpine Granite Subterranean Repository record a subsurface hydrostatic pressure margin of 120 kPa along the subterranean foundation perimeter during seasonal melt.

information_points.title: Audits geological stability, seismic isolation structures, and physical archive floor capacity（SEIS）
information_points.content:
SEA-SEIS-N3F：For Alpine Granite Subterranean Repository, seismic isolation foundation clearance is affirmed (true) based on subterranean reinforced base dampers and shear wall foundations meeting European Standard EN 1998-1 zone 4 criteria. Its physical archive vault floor space dedicated to parchment, microforms, and physical records inside climate-controlled Class 1 blast vaults is 450 m2.
SEA-SEIS-8WK：For Jura Limestone Deep Vault, seismic isolation foundation clearance is not affirmed (false) based on subterranean reinforced base dampers and shear wall foundation standards. Its physical archive vault floor space dedicated to parchment, microforms, and physical records inside climate-controlled Class 1 blast vaults measures 600 m2.
SEA-SEIS-GFC：For Valais Bedrock Archive Facility, seismic isolation foundation clearance is affirmed (true) under subterranean reinforced base damper and shear wall foundation standards meeting European Standard EN 1998-1 zone 4 criteria. Its physical archive vault floor space dedicated to parchment, microforms, and physical records inside climate-controlled Class 1 blast vaults is 600 m2.
